subject: AI & Agents
title: AI-Generated Faces That Don't Exist
description: A micro-lesson that makes AI-Generated Faces That Don't Exist usable.

hook.text: Visit 'This Person Does Not Exist' and see a photorealistic face of someone who was never born.

buildup.text: GANs generate human faces by learning the statistical distribution of real face photographs.

discovery.text: StyleGAN controls features independently — hair, age, skin tone, expression — with stunning precision.

twist.text: These fake faces are used for fraud, fake profiles, and propaganda. The misuse potential is vast.

climax.text: Detection is possible but imperfect — artifacts around ears and teeth sometimes give fakes away.

punchline.text: A face so real it's fake. A fake so real it's dangerous.

quiz.question: What is 'This Person Does Not Exist'?
options: A website showing GAN-generated photorealistic faces

details.summary: Generative adversarial networks can create photorealistic human faces that belong to no real person. These synthetic faces raise questions about trust, identity, and digital deception.
details.whyItMatters: Fake faces are already used in scams, fake profiles, and propaganda. Recognizing synthetic imagery is becoming a critical digital literacy skill for everyone.
takeaways: GANs generate photorealistic faces of nonexistent people
Synthetic faces are used in scams and disinformation
Detection tools exist but lag behind generation quality

faq.question: How does AI create faces that look completely real?
faq.answer: Generative adversarial networks pit two neural networks against each other. One generates faces while the other judges realism, iterating until the fakes are nearly indistinguishable from photographs.

faq.question: Can you tell if a face was generated by AI?
faq.answer: Sometimes. Clues include asymmetric earrings, blurred backgrounds, and irregular teeth. However, newer models fix these flaws, making manual detection increasingly difficult.
